data.name: Ferreby
data.gender_notes: Ferreby is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek words 'fero' meaning 'to bear' and 'by' meaning 'a boat'. The name Ferreby was given to those who guided boats across bodies of water. This name was commonly used in medieval Europe and is now considered a rare and unique name for a boy. The name Ferreby carries the meaning “Little ferryman” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Ferreby usually hope their child will grow to embody little ferryman and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_latin.name: Ferreby
in_latin.long_meaning: Ferreby is derived from Old English words 'ferr' or 'fere' meaning iron and 'by' meaning place or settlement. This name likely refers to a place known for its iron deposits or significant ironworking activities. Historically, such names were common in medieval England, reflecting local geography or industry.
